claims.text: Dynamic plasticity in solidified FeNiCrMn is primarily governed by scale-dependent slip avalanches.
Decreasing temperature produces larger and more abrupt slip events in FeNiCrMn.
Increasing strain rate produces larger and more abrupt slip events in FeNiCrMn.
Dislocation interactions trigger the slip events that control the macroscopic stress response.
The proposed solidified FeNiCrMn material has a homogenized microstructure with minimal secondary phases and a standard dislocation density.
The evolving dislocation network and localized slip bands collectively produce avalanche-like plastic events.
Applied strain and temperature modulate activation barriers for dislocation motion.
Slip-event sizes follow a power-law distribution whose cutoff shifts with temperature and strain rate.
Lower temperatures and higher strain rates favor larger but fewer slip avalanches.
Higher temperatures and lower strain rates favor smaller and more frequent slip events.
At lower temperature and higher strain rate, FeNiCrMn will exhibit pronounced stress drops and burst-like plastic deformation.
At higher temperature and lower strain rate, FeNiCrMn deformation will become more homogeneous and shift toward smaller slip avalanches.
Prior related high-entropy-alloy studies established a characteristic intermediate-condition stress–strain response with moderate stress drops and a typical slip-avalanche size distribution.
The proposed mechanism is applicable only when deformation is dominated by dislocation motion rather than twinning or phase transformations.
Local compositional fluctuations or minor secondary phases may influence avalanche statistics.
Slip avalanches appear to be dominant in related alloy systems.
The contribution of other deformation mechanisms in FeNiCrMn has not been fully quantified.
